body: Gravity Rush 2 is Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 action-adventure, first released in Australia and Europe on 18 January 2017. Kat is drawn away from Hekseville and reaches another world, where the floating city of Jirga Para Lhao introduces new people and inequalities. Her ability to change gravity lets her fall toward a chosen direction rather than remain fixed to the ground. The sequel builds its exploration around that movement, filling the space above, below and between streets with routes that can be approached from several sides.

Alongside Kat's familiar gravity style, Lunar makes her lighter and more agile, while Jupiter gives movement and attacks a heavier impact. Changing styles alters how a jump, approach or strike feels without changing the person being controlled. The player can match that weight to a particular threat or passage through the city. Gravity powers also allow nearby objects to become projectiles. A street therefore offers material for the next fight as well as a surface to leave behind when Kat chooses another direction to fall.

Jirga Para Lhao's busy streets and distinct districts expand the social world around Kat, giving her people to meet and local tasks to complete between larger events. The scale of its floating architecture provides a practical reason to experiment with gravity, while the story follows the divisions within the city. Keiichiro Toyama returned as director, with Kohei Tanaka composing the music. The sequel developed the first game's central movement rather than replacing it, showing how the same power could support a broader world and more varied encounters.
